A's two neighbors are linked, so A scores 1.00, then B and D 0.67, C 0.50 and E 0.33. Nodes with fewer than two neighbors get 0 rather than None, so the pendant G ties with F at 0." width="100%"} The clustering coefficient measures the degree to which a node's neighbors are connected to each other. For a node `v`: `C(v) = (number of edges between neighbors) / (number of possible edges between neighbors) = (2 × triangles through v) / (degree(v) × (degree(v) - 1))` On a directed graph this is Fagiolo's directed clustering, which counts every directed triangle through `v` whatever the directions of its arcs (see `local_clustering_coefficient()` for the formula); it matches `networkx.clustering()`. Parallel edges and self-loops are ignored. Returns `0.0` for nodes with degree < `2` (cannot form triangles). Range: `[0, 1]` where: - `0` = neighbors are not connected at all - `1` = neighbors form a complete graph (clique) ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store clustering coefficient values. If `None`, uses `clustering_coefficient` as the attribute name. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary mapping node IDs to clustering coefficients. If `False`, stores values as node attributes and returns the Graph for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float] or Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to clustering coefficients (`0.0` to `1.0`). If `return_dict=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The local clustering coefficient $C(v) = \dfrac{2\,\Delta(v)}{k(v)(k(v) - 1)}$ (with $\Delta(v)$ the number of triangles\ containing $v$ and $k(v)$ its degree) counts the fraction of possible edges among $v$'s neighbors that actually exist. Values near $1$ mean the neighborhood is essentially a clique. Values near $0$ mean it is tree-like. Averaging $C(v)$ across the graph produces the network-level statistic Watts and Strogatz (1998) used to identify small-world structure: high local clustering combined with short average path lengths. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Storing values as attributes (the default) still lets you read them back afterward. All three nodes here get a coefficient of `1.0`, since a triangle's neighbors are already fully connected to each other: ::: {#3ecdc306 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) .clustering_coefficient() ) graph.get_node_attrs("clustering_coefficient") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {2: 1.0, 3: 1.0, 1: 1.0} ``` ::: ::: In a star graph, none of the spokes connect to each other, so the hub's coefficient is `0.0` even though it has several neighbors: ::: {#c8dc6fab .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["center", "A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("center", "A"), ("center", "B"), ("center", "C")]) ) clustering = graph.clustering_coefficient(return_dict=True) center_id = graph.get_id_from_label("center") clustering[center_id] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0.0 ``` ::: :::
